learning_outcomes.text: Propose and calculate integrals of single-variable functions and apply them to solve real problems.
Propose and calculate integrals of two- and three-variable functions, and apply them to solve real problems.
Use methods that allow approximating the derivative and the definite integral of a function.
Use the parametrizations of the main curves and surfaces to apply them to integration problems.
Fluently handle various kinds of sets and measures, and acquire sufficient abstraction capacity to frame previous knowledge on integration within a broader framework.
Interpret the concept of Fourier series and transform, their calculation, properties, and applications.
Solve advanced Calculus problems using computer tools.

syllabus_topics: Unit 1. Introduction to the concept of integral
Unit 2. Extension of the concept of integral
Integration over a measure: Lebesgue integral
teaching_methods: Virtual expository sessions (videos, presentations, instructional texts, self-assessment questionnaires)
Presential expository classes (doubt resolution, theoretical results, examples)
Virtual classroom practices (videos, questionnaires, forum participation)
Presential classroom practices (individual/group exercises and tasks)
Virtual laboratory practices (solving exercises with MatLab)
Presential laboratory practices (solving exercises with MatLab)
Tutorials (Teams chat, Campus Virtual forums, personal or group tutorials via Teams)

assessment_methods.method: Written Exams (NC) (weighted average of P1 and P2 or Global Exam)

assessment_rules: The final grade (NF) is calculated as: NF = 0.2 NL + 0.2 NA + 0.5 NC + 0.1 NCv. The course is passed if NF >= 5, NC >= 3.5, and NL >= 3.5. If these minimums are not met, the final grade will be min(NF, NC, NL). For differentiated evaluation, if classroom practices cannot be evaluated, NF = 0.2 NL + 0.6 NC + 0.2 NOL. In extraordinary calls, students can retake an exam for NC and/or a laboratory practice test for NL, replacing the previous grade for that part; NA and NCv grades are conserved.
